name: The Nerve Agents
label: Revelation
lede: A former Marine named his band after the chemical weapons he'd trained against, put eyeliner on a Bay Area hardcore band, and walked away at its peak two weeks before his daughter was born.

eras.title: One show before Los Angeles
eras.text: Eric Ozenne of Redemption 87 and Unit Pride had six months left in San Francisco before a planned move south. The band he started to fill them turned into a Revelation signing before the six months were up.

years.h: Eric Ozenne names a band after chemical weapons
years.p: Eric Ozenne impulsively asks Andy Granelli of Model American if he's ready to start a band, meaning to play one show before moving to LA. The name comes from nerve agents, which Ozenne learned about in Marine Corps chemical warfare training.

years.h: The Nerve Agents' demo reaches Jordan Cooper at Revelation
years.p: Paul Miner records the demo at Cold Front Records. It gets to Revelation co-founder Jordan Cooper, and Revelation signs the band.
Eight songs of fast, yelled San Francisco hardcore. It goes out of print and stays off vinyl for more than 25 years.

eras.title: Eyeliner and the White Owl
eras.text: A new bassist brought piano and the band started wearing eyeliner, pulling Siouxsie and the Banshees and 45 Grave into hardcore. The shows turned frenzied, chaotic and sometimes violent, and punk and hardcore crowds started showing up to the same room.

q: We wanted everyone there to know that we welcomed everyone
years.h: Dante Sigona joins The Nerve Agents, and out comes the eyeliner
years.p: Bassist Matt Sweirs leaves and Dante Sigona replaces him. The band adopts eyeliner and darker influences like [[Dead Kennedys|37c78aeb-d196-42b5-b991-6afb4fc9bc2e]], [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]] and Siouxsie.

years.h: The Nerve Agents cut their album at Art of Ears, Hayward
years.p: The Nerve Agents record Days of the White Owl with engineer Andy Ernst in Hayward, California.

years.h: A split with Kill Your Idols on Mankind
years.p: The Nerve Agents share a record with Long Island's [[Kill Your Idols|b6154aed-416f-43bf-93fe-0906b051535f]]. Sessions Records also collects early songs as The Way It Should Be...

years.src: Wikipedia: Days of the White Owl
years.p: Sixteen songs, most under two and a half minutes, bookended by piano pieces Dante Sigona wrote. [[Davey Havok|0d7bf43a-d747-4c8b-bc4c-927d9a7fe03a]] of [[AFI|1c3919b2-43ca-4a4a-935d-9d50135ec0ef]] guests, and Evil is a [[45 Grave|337027f4-4f29-42f4-bc4d-63e7d4e74e1a]] cover.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia some critics knocked the album for a lack of originality, but hardcore and punk fans took to its speed and hooks.

years.h: On tour with AFI, Agnostic Front and The Business
years.p: The Nerve Agents tour California and the East Coast with [[AFI|1c3919b2-43ca-4a4a-935d-9d50135ec0ef]], join the Spirit of the Streets tour with F-Minus, [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]] and The Business, and play dates with [[T.S.O.L.|e3207b63-ab05-42bc-924e-b1299b89c406]]
years.xp: Ozenne says Long Beach's PCH Club became a second home, and the band's Bay Area shows merged punk and hardcore audiences who didn't usually share a floor. Wikipedia describes the sets as frenzied, chaotic and often violent, with theatrical costumes.

years.h: Full set at 924 Gilman Street, Berkeley, August 26, 2000
yt: Full set at 924 Gilman Street, Berkeley, August 26, 2000

eras.title: Out on a high note
eras.text: A move to Tim Armstrong's Hellcat put The Nerve Agents on Epitaph's distribution, and the band was drawing bigger than ever. Inside, it was falling apart.

years.p: Back at Art of Ears with Andy Ernst, The Nerve Agents make angular, melodic songs mostly under two minutes. [[Jade Puget|535ae49b-d6a5-4527-a375-3a7d96022194]] of AFI adds backing vocals on one track. Punknews and AllMusic both give it 2.5 stars.

q: Probably best that we went out on a high note.
years.h: The Nerve Agents end at The Pound in San Francisco
years.p: A conflict between Eric Ozenne and Dante Sigona ends in an ultimatum. The band's last run is five December shows with [[Lars Frederiksen and the Bastards|f3a090bf-6173-42d7-86f5-7fcdeaabfc58]], ending at The Pound on December 30.
years.xp: Ozenne lost his voice during those final shows. His daughter Grace was born two weeks after the breakup, and he says fatherhood was the priority.

eras.title: The Distillers and White Fence
eras.text: The Nerve Agents scattered into some of the better-known bands of the next decade.

years.h: Andy Granelli to The Distillers; Tim Presley to White Fence
years.p: Drummer Andy Granelli plays in [[The Distillers|d25fa5a6-92bf-46a3-8bf7-31149b62eb84]] and, with guitarist Tim Presley, [[Darker My Love|15c5c0de-b8ff-49ab-8a58-506c89453f03]]. Presley goes on to White Fence.

eras.title: Reissues, not reunions
eras.text: Revelation brought the whole catalog back, including the Hellcat album. The band stayed broken up.

years.h: Revelation reissues all three Nerve Agents records
years.p: Revelation's Adam Lentz pitched the anniversary reissues around 2020; Epitaph licensed The Butterfly Collection for three years. The 1998 EP gets its first vinyl pressing. Ozenne says there's no hope of reunion shows.
